reconcile.note: Clarke reads Moses's natural slowness of speech as compatible with the God-empowered might in word and deed that Stephen credits him with.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells notes the two verses hand Moses opposite verbal abilities, disclaiming eloquence in Exodus yet mighty in words in Acts.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Was Moses a good speaker?"

sides.snippet: I am not eloquent, neither before now, nor since you have spoken to your servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.
sides.verseText: Moses said to Yahweh, \"Oh, Lord, I am not eloquent, neither before now, nor since you have spoken to your servant; for I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue.\"

sides.snippet: He was mighty in his words and works.
sides.verseText: Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians. He was mighty in his words and works.
